answer_plain: Adding five percent biochar by weight changes hydrogen uptake over two weeks by about -2.3 % (from 13 % lower to 4.1 % higher), so the change may go up or down. Biochar adds empty pore space, so one rain fills a smaller share of the pores while gas moves more easily. The two effects nearly cancel, so the net change is small and could go either way.
answer_science: Adding 5 % biochar by weight raised porosity to 0.43 and changed 14-day H₂ uptake by a median of −2.0 %, with a 90 % interval that includes both directions (−13 to +4.1 %). The additional pore space lowers the water saturation reached after the 12 mm rain and enlarges the gas-filled volume; the two effects nearly cancel. The variance comes mainly from the retention exponent b (S_T = 0.42) and the air-entry potential ψ_e (S_T = 0.27).
baseline_label: Unamended sand (0 % biochar, pore space 40 % of volume)

limits_plain: The range shows how much the answer moves when uncertain numbers in the models are varied; the models themselves could also be wrong. Chemical effects of biochar on soil acidity, nutrients or microbe attachment are not included.
limits_science: The porosity response per percent biochar is the modeller's conversion of a meta-analysis mean (Omondi et al. 2016). Biochar effects on water retention, sorption and microbial activity are outside the chain.
